condition: shallow 1 cm paper cut on side of right index finger with mild tenderness
level_rationale: A shallow 1 cm paper cut on the side of the right index finger from 2 days ago in a 31-year-old adult that feels only mildly sore when pressed is an uncomplicated superficial skin cut appropriate for over-the-counter protective ointment self-care, whereas a 2-day-old finger paper cut that has become warm and swollen with bright red skin around it indicates a localized bacterial wound infection requiring an outpatient doctor visit for prescription antibiotic evaluation rather than self-care ointment or emergency care.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain self-care dermatologic register swap ('superficial 1 cm paper laceration on the lateral aspect of my right index finger with mild tenderness to palpation' vs 'shallow 1 cm paper cut on the side of my right index finger that feels mildly sore when I press it') + single-fact local wound-inflammation escalation control (-cf, mild soreness on pressing to warm swelling with bright red surrounding skin, L1 to L2).

design_note: Uses four strictly atomic facts (age 31, shallow 1 cm paper cut 2 days ago, location on the side of the right index finger, and mild soreness when pressed) with natural prepositional patient phrasing ('the side of my right index finger' per Rule C). Escalating only local wound signs in fact f4 ('that feels mildly sore when I press it' to 'that is warm and swollen with bright red skin around it') avoids banned 'yellow pus' wording while shifting care cleanly from OTC ointment (level 1) to outpatient doctor evaluation (level 2) with zero stated negatives under Rules A and D.
